steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Up ahead is the junction between Syndicate and the Rust. Why do you bring me here?
Gravel and rubble along the road forces you to leave the car and continue on foot. Anne follows you with a medical kit slung over her back, not knowing your intentions.
test
test
test
test
test
test
I've heard that you're good with kids, so I take you out for this field mission. It's also a break for me.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: I'm sorry, I've been restless lately. I've caused trouble for everyone at the medical department.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: But what are you going to do when you find a Maniac? Eliminate them, or...
I just want to ask him a question for my friend.
Anne realizes what you mean. During your conversations, you tacitly avoid the cause of Anne's anxiety—the Corruptor remains in the SALVA's basement.
These are all you found? But this is a boy.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: The sheriffs at Syndicate don't have the habit of recording their duties. All the info you want for "the Maniac of the same age as Paige" are here.
Forget it. Give it a try. I hope she will make a reasonable choice this time.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: What exactly are you trying to do? Don't you need to bring along a guard?
No, I'll go with Anne alone.
The adjutant is still looking at you with distrust.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Every time you show up with a Sinner after an interrogation, you do something out of line.
You follow the map Nightingale gave you all the way west, but don't encounter the little boy described by the sheriff.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: We can't go any further. The Rust is up ahead, and there are roaming Corruptors everywhere. It would be hard for the two of us to come back alive.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: It's getting dark soon. I'm afraid it's not very safe here either.
Maybe he left temporarily for something?
With his physical condition as a Maniac, he shouldn't be able to go too far.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Perhaps we came too late, and he's already...
Before Anne can finish, there is a sudden rustling sound from behind the crooked tree.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: And who's that?
I should be the one asking you.
A hooded boy emerges, his back against the setting sun. The hood obscures his face.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Are you the Maniac the sheriff told us about? Great, you're still alive!
Ha. Open your eyes and take a good look.
The boy takes off his hood.
Even though you have seen quite a few monsters, his mutated state still makes you both gasp.
Sixty percent of his body is covered with dark pus. His skin can no longer resist corruption and has begun to rot.
Without his hood, his mutations are terrifying.

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: Hey, what's wrong with that woman in white? Why is she staring at me like that? It's annoying.

options: Maybe you remind her of an old friend.
Didn't you tell her to take a good look?

choices.text: Maybe you remind her of an old friend.
Didn't you tell her to take a good look?

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: Is that why you come to find me?

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: Pfff... are you here to see me?

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: I'm here to help you!
Anne lowers her head and rummages through the medical kit.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: The wounds on your body must be very painful. I have painkillers and anesthetics here!

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Don't worry, they're all tailored for Syndrome Mania, they can definitely...

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: Got anything sweet to eat?

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Let me see...
She actually finds a lollipop in her bag.

options: Why do you carry lollipops around with you?

choices.text: Why do you carry lollipops around with you?

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: It's a habit I picked up from the prevention and control site. When kids don't want to take their shots, I coax them with lollipops.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: It's a bit melted though. Is that alright?

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: That's fine, toss it over. Let me have a taste.
The boy catches the lollipop, unwraps it clumsily, and gives it a lick.

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: Hmm... So this is the taste.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Hmm...

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: Why are you still here? It's getting dark.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Is there anything else I can help you with?

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: Anything else? Yes actually. I want to go to see Eastside. I heard it's a dazzling place with lots to eat and drink, and nobody goes Maniac...

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: But I definitely can't enter with this look.

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: It's probably better for me to take adventures in the Rust.

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: From there, I might be able to catch a glimpse of Eastside from afar.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Do you have...any other wishes?
Anne doesn't go on, but you know what she wants to ask.

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: Duh! You think I want to die? But I'm already like this...

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Wait! What if one day Maniacs can be cured?

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: What will happen after I'm cured? I'll still be a monster, right? Will they let me in Eastside?
The boy's tone is unusually calm.

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: As you say, it's only "what if." I can tell from your gloomy look that you're bluffing.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: ...I'm sorry.

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: Um, what are you apologizing for?

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: As a healthcare worker, I cannot fulfill your wish to live.

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: Stop flattering yourself! At most, you can make my heart beat again. That doesn't count as fulfilling a wish.
The boy bites the lollipop in annoyance.

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: It's boring to live just for the sake of staying alive...

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: There are just many things that I haven't done yet. But what does that have to do with you?
The boy's words seem to remind Anne of something. She gazes quietly at the child who outshines her in maturity, and stays silent for a long time.

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: Don't do anything weird to me! If it's just a beating heart, I don't want it.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Don't worry, it won't. It won't beat again...

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: What?

steps.speaker: Paige
steps.content: Anne, why do you become a nurse?

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Because Syndicate has poor medical conditions. I had to go to Eastside to learn nursing and bring back the knowledge to help everyone.

steps.speaker: Patient
steps.content: Ah! So Anne is from Syndicate. That must be tough.

steps.speaker: Patient
steps.content: I'm not that ambitious. I just want to make a name for myself in a gang. But I don't dare to touch those strange weapons anymore.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Really? Then who was the one swearing to become rich?

steps.speaker: Patient
steps.content: Eh? Wasn't it the internist?

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: Me? I just want to return to Eastside after finishing my volunteer work. My wife is still waiting for me.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: What about Paige? What do you want to do when you grow up?

steps.speaker: Paige
steps.content: Anything! As long as I can be with Anne!

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Hahaha, what kind of wish is that?

steps.speaker: Paige
steps.content: What are you laughing at! I'm serious! Cough cough cough...

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Alright, Miss Tag-Along, it's time to take your medicine. Open your mouth...

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: If I've promised to save you, but failed to do so, and your dream could not be realized, would you really not blame me?

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: You're so annoying! Didn't you ask that already? I told you, it has nothing to do with you.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Okay...
The boy looks at absent-minded Anne impatiently.

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: Hey, is she okay? Why is she crying and laughing?
It seems like she's already got the answer.
She looks at you with both gratitude and guilt.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Chief, thank you for taking me out today. But what I'm going to do next may cause you some trouble, so please forgive me...
She walks over to the boy, opens her bag, and fishes out each item one by one to explain.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Can you see this clearly?

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: What... what are you going to do?

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: This is a serum I crafted with my power, which can delay your mutation. One injection every morning and evening should be enough to support you another month.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: This is the painkiller that Iron made.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: I know the spread of Mania is very painful. This will make you feel a bit better...

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Lastly...
Anne zips up the bag, stands up and picks up her weapon.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: This will help you leave immediately... without pain.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: You can choose between extending your final days to complete what you've always wanted to do, or the syringe in my hand...
Anne...
She aims the weapon at the boy. Her face is unusually devoid of smiles, with a look of calm ruthlessness.
But both you and the boy can see that Anne's hands are shaking.

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: A month? ...That's fine too.
The boy picks up the medicine from the ground.

options: Are you going to let him go?
Don't you have a third option?

choices.text: Are you going to let him go?
Don't you have a third option?

steps.content: Anne purses her lips and lowers her head to avoid your gaze.
Are you really going to let this kid go? In the eyes of the FAC, it is a serious dereliction of duty to let go of a Maniac.
Put him in the special potion. He's our new hope.
Anne doesn't speak. She purses her lips and lowers her head to avoid your gaze.
It seems like she's already made a new choice. Are you really going to let this kid go? Even at the cost of malfeasance...
You can't guarantee that he won't ever hurt anyone.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Chief, didn't you bring me out here to let me make a choice? Why...
Not on this matter.
You prepare to step forward to attack, but suddenly you feel a stab in the back of your neck.
You!...
You black out and fall into Anne's arms.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Chief, I won't run away, but... sorry, this kid still wants to see the world.
Confused, you overhear Anne's last words to the boy.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Never get yourself caught by the Bureau. Go to the Rust and run far away from here.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: I wish you luck for your last month. I hope we... won't see each other again...
Let's go back to the MBCC. Anne, nothing happened today.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: You will be blamed...
I know.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: I won't let you take the blame.
Anne takes out a syringe from her pocket.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: This is anesthesia. I won't hurt you or run away.
You'll take the insensible me back to the MBCC and take all the blame yourself.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: ...That's the best solution I can think of.
She wants to take all the blame herself again.
You never thought that I'd agree to let him go?

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: It is your duty to eliminate Maniacs...
But that kid still wants to see the world. That's what "to live" means for him.
Anne looks at you in surprise. The anesthetic syringe in her hand falls to the ground and breaks in two.
You hope that you can do more than just "persistence" to eliminate Mania. So do I.

options: Tell the boy to stay away from others.

choices.text: Tell the boy to stay away from others.

steps.content: In your final month, you can go to the Rust, but stay away from other humans. Don't congregate with the Corruptors either. If you hurt someone and get discovered by the FAC, I really can't help you.

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: Got it! Thanks!
The boy waves the leftover lollipop in his hand. You and Anne watch him turn around and disappear into the distance.

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: My name is Gary! If you get the chance, go visiting Eastside for me!
